dataset.description:
The main tasks are:
1) to expand the scope of MuLaR corpus data, obtaining 5-10 hours of audio recordings (interviews), transcribing and inserting into the Latgalian speech corpus (taking into account ethical aspects and implementing previous practice, interviews will be conducted after obtaining informed consent, personal data will be pseudonymized);
2) to perform corpus data visualisation by spatiotemporal model design.

distribution.title:
MuLaR is a Latgalian spoken language corpus. It includes: 1) interviews conducted during field work; 2) audio recordings of TV (Latgales Reģionālā televīzija) and radio (Latvijas Radio) broadcasts; 3) speech recordings of Latgalians living in Siberia (2017-2018); 4) Latgalian audio recordings and transcriptions of the TriMCo Dialect Corpus project. The transcriptions of the audio recordings were made using the ELAN software; an orthographic transcription was used that preserves dialect features. Each audio recording is accompanied by metadata: the location and time of the recording, the duration of the audio segment, the speaker's gender and age. 
Research results achieved within the Project can make a major contribution to the recognition of the status and preservation of the Latgalian language, promoting awareness of its unique characteristics as one of the historical regional variants of the Latvian language. The expansion of MuLaR and the integration of spatiotemporal metadata into the corpus will open wider opportunities for its further use as a resource in synchronic and diachronic geospatial, ethnographic, and sociolinguistic research on the development, use, and preservation of Latgalian.

dataset.title: LCS FARP Latgalian speech corpus (MuLaR) data

dmp.description: The goal of the research project is to design a prototype of a spatiotemporal model for conducting efficient multifaceted analysis of a corpus of contemporary Latgalian speech (MuLaR) for multifunctional application of the corpus; to promote interdisciplinary cooperation and advance both individual and institutional research capacity.
